title: Distribution-Value Coevolution for Adaptive RLHF Data Scheduling

problem.claim: RLHF training data must be scheduled while both model capabilities and data utility evolve over time.

gap.claim: Existing pipelines use fixed or uniform sampling and treat data value as static, an assumption the authors characterize as flawed.

contributions.claim: The paper identifies and formalizes the Distribution-Value Coevolution principle, in which data value emerges dynamically from interactions between data characteristics and the model's evolving capability boundary.

The paper operationalizes the principle through a unified adaptive scheduling framework combining distribution-level organization, sliding-window influence estimation, and bandit-guided resource allocation.
The proposed approach reports performance improvements on AIME24 for Llama3.2-3B and gains across models ranging from 1B to 7B parameters.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments report up to a 57.1% relative improvement, or 8.9% absolute improvement, on AIME24 for Llama3.2-3B.
Experiments report gains for models ranging from 1B to 7B parameters.

narrative_sequence.summary: RLHF is presented as central to aligning LLMs with human intent.
The paper raises the question of how to schedule training data as model capabilities and data utility evolve.
Fixed or uniform sampling treats data value as static, which the authors describe as fundamentally flawed.
The paper proposes that data value coevolves with the model's capability boundary and motivates adaptive curriculum design.
A three-component framework implements adaptive scheduling, and experiments report improvements across benchmark and model settings.

unknowns: No experimental baselines, datasets beyond AIME24, statistical uncertainty, or ablation details are provided.
The abstract does not specify the exact exploration-exploitation guarantees or scheduling algorithm.
